prompt: Create a new 2D planar DC magnetostatic model. All coordinates and dimensions are in millimeters. Use out-of-plane depth 20 mm. Make a circular conductor centered at (0,0), radius 1 mm, relative permeability 1; label (0,0). Put it on a DC circuit of +1 A with +1 turn. Use a circular air domain centered at (0,0), radius 10 mm, A=0 on its boundary and background air label (5,0). Probe B at (2,0). Use global mesh size 0.5 mm. No force extraction is requested.

Create a 2D planar DC magnetic model. All coordinates are in millimeters; out-of-plane depth is 10 mm. Create an asymmetric C-shaped core using these polygon vertices in order: (-15,-12), (10,-12), (10,-6), (-7,-6), (-7,6), (6,6), (6,12), (-15,12). Use linear relative permeability 1000 and place its label at (-12,0). Add two rectangular winding cross-sections, both with relative permeability 1: from (-5,-4) to (0,4), label (-2.5,0), +50 turns; and from (-22,-4) to (-17,4), label (-19.5,0), -50 turns. Assign both to the same circuit carrying 1 A DC. Use an enclosing air rectangle from (-40,-30) to (30,30), with A=0 on its boundary and air label at (20,20). Use a global mesh size of 1 mm. Measure magnetic flux density at (3,0).

Create an axisymmetric DC magnetic model of a finite air-core winding. All coordinates are in millimeters, x is radius r and y is axial z; use a full revolution with no planar depth. Its rectangular r-z winding cross-section runs from r=20 mm to r=30 mm and z=-20 mm to z=20 mm. Use relative permeability 1, +200 turns, a 1 A DC circuit, label (25,0), and winding mesh 0.5 mm. Surround it with air r=0 to 160 mm, z=-160 to 160 mm, A=0 on the exterior boundary, background air label (120,120), and global mesh 4 mm. Probe the field on the axis at (0,0), (0,20), and (0,50).

Create a planar DC magnetic model in millimeters with out-of-plane depth 5 mm. Use a reusable fourfold rotational pattern of identical circular winding cross-sections. The first circle is centered at (5,0) with radius 0.5 mm; rotate it by 90 degrees around (0,0) for each of four instances. Place each winding label at its center. All four windings have relative permeability 1, +1 turn, and share a circuit carrying +1 A DC. Use a circular air domain centered at (0,0), radius 20 mm, A=0 on its boundary, background air label (15,0), and global mesh 0.5 mm. Probe B at (0,0). Preserve the repeated component/feature relationship so it can be edited as one pattern.

Create a planar DC magnetic model, all coordinates in millimeters, out-of-plane depth 10 mm. The rectangular iron core extends from (-8,-8) to (-2,8), with label (-5,0). Its relative permeability and B-H curve are unknown; do not assume a value. A separate rectangular winding extends from (0,-4) to (4,4), label (2,0), relative permeability 1, +20 turns on a circuit carrying 1 A DC. The air domain is (-20,-20) to (20,20), with A=0 on its boundary, air label (15,15), and global mesh 1 mm. Probe B at (8,0). Preserve the core and winding in the component hierarchy, identify the missing physical input, and ask for it before numerical execution.

Develop a 2D planar model of an interior permanent-magnet motor in millimeters with axial depth 20 mm. Decompose it into stator, rotor, shaft, windings and air gap. Stator outer radius is 30 mm and bore radius 20 mm, with 12 slots. Rotor outer radius is 19 mm and shaft radius 5 mm. The rotor has eight poles with buried V-shaped magnet pairs, remanence 1.2 T. The steel requires a nonlinear B-H law, and the air gap must support rotation. The detailed V angles, magnet thicknesses, slot contour dimensions, winding excitation and B-H data are not yet supplied. Preserve a custom rotor component and these unsupported or missing requirements explicitly. Show the available hierarchy and geometry intent without inventing those physical values or replacing permanent magnets and nonlinear steel with a linear air-core model.
